content: Valganciclovir should be stored properly to maintain its effectiveness. Tablets should be kept at room temperature, away from light and moisture. The liquid form of this medication must be refrigerated but should not be frozen. Do not dispose of this medication by flushing it down the toilet or pouring it into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. When the medication is expired or no longer needed, it should be discarded properly. Before starting valganciclovir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you have any allergies to this medication, ganciclovir, acyclovir, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Valganciclovir may cause dizziness or drowsiness, which can be worsened by alcohol or marijuana. Limit your consumption of alcoholic beverages. This medication can increase your susceptibility to infections or worsen existing ones. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Inform your healthcare provider that you are taking valganciclovir before receiving any vaccinations or immunizations. During pregnancy, valganciclovir should only be used if absolutely necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss the potential risks and benefits with your doctor. Women of childbearing age should undergo a pregnancy test before starting this medication. To prevent pregnancy, men with female partners should use effective barrier protection, such as latex or polyurethane condoms, during treatment and for at least 90 days after stopping the medication. Women of childbearing age should use reliable birth control methods, such as oral contraceptives and condoms, during treatment and for at least 30 days after discontinuing the medication. It is not known if this medication passes into breast milk, but due to potential risks to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using valganciclovir. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of valganciclovir or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all medications and products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. Some drugs, such as cancer chemotherapy, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, zidovudine, or cyclosporine, may decrease bone marrow function, lower blood cell counts, or cause kidney problems, which could interact with valganciclovir. Note that valganciclovir is very similar to ganciclovir, so these medications should not be used together. If someone overdoses on valganciclovir and experiences severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. While taking valganciclovir, regular medical and laboratory tests, such as complete blood counts, kidney function tests, and eye exams, should be conducted to monitor your health and the medication's effects. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about valganciclovir. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs.
